summary: GPT-5.4 nano has no OpenAI system card or model card, so the closest owner documentation is OpenAI's API model page. That page presents it as a small GPT-5.4-class model for high-volume helper tasks with a 400,000-token context window, image input, text output, and a March 17, 2026 snapshot; GitHub treats it as a utility model rather than a selectable Copilot CLI or app model.

capabilities.text: OpenAI's model page identifies the `gpt-5.4-nano-2026-03-17` snapshot and positions GPT-5.4 nano for simple high-volume tasks such as classification, extraction, ranking, and sub-agent work.
The page states a 400,000-token context window, 128,000 maximum output tokens, an August 31, 2025 knowledge cutoff, and reasoning-token support.
The page lists text input/output and image input, with audio and video not supported.
The page lists function calling, structured outputs, streaming, and several Responses API tools, while marking fine-tuning, computer use, and tool search as unsupported.

limitations.text: No publisher system card or model card exists for GPT-5.4 nano, and the GPT-5.4 Thinking card does not mention nano.
The owner page does not provide benchmark tables, red-team results, Preparedness classifications, or safety mitigations comparable to a system card.
GitHub marks GPT-5.4 nano unavailable in Copilot clients except the Codex extension for VS Code, so it is not a selectable Copilot CLI or app model.

practical_implications.text: Treat GPT-5.4 nano as utility infrastructure in Copilot rather than a model to select for normal CLI or app conversations.
Do not transfer GPT-5.4 Thinking's card findings or benchmark scores to GPT-5.4 nano.
Use ordinary tests and review for any visible output from workflows that may rely on this model.

coverage_notes: No publisher system card or model card exists. This digest uses OpenAI's GPT-5.4 nano model page and the catalog's availability note, and it records that the GPT-5.4 Thinking card does not mention nano.
